did: Reshaped the first part of Rust Rounds' essay opening into the conversation the owner approved. Someone new to Rust Rounds asks up to three questions in a voice of its own, and the owner's newest recording of each answer plays, reused week to week until they record again. The questions and answers are one standing set kept in the code, held to two to three minutes across the answers, whose words the owner approved with one change, "split" for "fork". Along the way it found that a week answered point by point could never become an essay, because the Monday routine never fetched those points' transcripts, and fixed that in a defect PR of its own.

calls.title: How a recording is reused week to week
options: Each answer's take keeps the week it was said in, and home picks the newest one of the same version
Every week's take of an answer shares one standing name
calls.why: It keeps each recording where it was said and keeps the rule that a week sends only its own takes; the coordinator agreed.
calls.undo: Give the opening one standing name, and let a week's send carry a take from any week.

calls.title: How the standing questions and answers change
options: A set kept in the code, changed only when the owner asks
The routine writes the set once, then copies it
The owner edits the set on the phone
calls.why: The owner wants a standing intro the routine doesn't rewrite; a set in the code changes only on purpose, and the owner approves its words.
calls.undo: Let the routine write the set when none exists and copy last week's after.

left: The server half of the opening, at contract epoch 25: it waits on epochs 23 and 24 reaching the server's main, and a fresh session takes it from the handover on #3269.
The phone's opening pages (part 2): a fresh session builds them once #3277 is on main, reading which recording is current and playing it from home.
Copying the standing set into each week waits on the routine writing the newer week format (#3272).
